name: ChatAFL
org: Nanyang Technological University, University of Melbourne
one_liner: Protocol-guided greybox fuzzer that uses an LLM to infer message grammars and mutate state-machine inputs under coverage feedback.

loop.proposes: An LLM extracts protocol request grammars and synthesizes structure-aware seed sequences and state-transition mutations.
loop.judged_by: The greybox fuzzer (AFLNet engine) executes the target network server, measuring edge coverage, state transitions, and sanitizer crashes.
loop.steers: When coverage stalls in a protocol state, the fuzzer queries the LLM with the observed server responses to generate inputs that unlock new states.

headline_result: Covered 47.6% more state transitions and 29.6% more code branches than AFLNet across nine network protocol implementations, discovering 9 previously unknown vulnerabilities.
caveat: Targets text-based application protocols (RTSP, FTP, SMTP, SIP); binary protocols require separate serialization adapters.
beyond_harness_note: The evolutionary greybox fuzzer runs the main coverage loop and calls the LLM only to infer protocol grammars and break coverage plateaus.
generative_model: LLM protocol grammar and seed mutator
algorithmic_authority: Coverage-guided stateful greybox fuzzer and address sanitizers

sources.title: Large Language Model Guided Protocol Fuzzing (NDSS 2024)

verification.notes: Checked against Meng et al., NDSS 2024.
